claim: T regulatory (Treg) cells play vital roles in modulating immunity and tissue homeostasis.
source: T regulatory (Treg) cells play vital roles in modulating immunity and tissue homeostasis.
evidence: This is a general statement about Treg cell function that draws from established scientific consensus.

claim: The actions of Treg cells depend on TCR recognition of peptide-MHC molecules.
source: Their actions depend on TCR recognition of peptide-MHC molecules
evidence: This statement is supported by established scientific knowledge about Treg cell function.

claim: The degree of peptide specificity of Treg-cell function is unknown.
source: yet the degree of peptide specificity of Treg-cell function, and whether Treg ligands can be used to manipulate Treg cell biology are unknown.
evidence: This is an explicit statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Whether Treg ligands can be used to manipulate Treg cell biology is unknown.
source: yet the degree of peptide specificity of Treg-cell function, and whether Treg ligands can be used to manipulate Treg cell biology are unknown.
evidence: This is an explicit statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: An Ab-peptide library was developed that enabled unbiased screening of peptides recognized by a bona fide murine Treg cell clone isolated from visceral adipose tissue (VAT).
source: Here, we developed an Ab-peptide library that enabled unbiased screening of peptides recognized by a bona fide murine Treg cell clone isolated from the visceral adipose tissue (VAT)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study describing the development of a screening platform.

claim: Surrogate agonist peptides with differing affinities and signaling potencies were identified.
source: and identified surrogate agonist peptides, with differing affinities and signaling potencies.
evidence: This is a primary finding describing the identification of peptides with varying properties.

claim: VAT-Treg cells expanded in vivo by one of the surrogate agonists preserved the typical VAT-Treg transcriptional programs.
source: The VAT-Treg cells expanded in vivo by one of the surrogate agonists preserved the typical VAT-Treg transcriptional programs.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by RNA-seq data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Immunization with the surrogate peptide expanded VAT-Treg cells.
source: Immunization with this surrogate, especially when coupled with blockade of TNFα signaling, expanded VAT-Treg cells
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by flow cytometry data in the manuscript.

claim: Immunization with the surrogate peptide resulted in protection from inflammation.
source: resulting in protection from inflammation and improved metabolic indices, including promotion of insulin sensitivity.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by immunocyte composition analysis in the manuscript.

claim: Immunization with the surrogate peptide improved metabolic indices, including promotion of insulin sensitivity.
source: resulting in protection from inflammation and improved metabolic indices, including promotion of insulin sensitivity.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by metabolic testing data (ITT, GTT, insulin levels) in the manuscript.

claim: Coupling surrogate peptide immunization with blockade of TNFα signaling enhanced VAT-Treg cell expansion.
source: Immunization with this surrogate, especially when coupled with blockade of TNFα signaling, expanded VAT-Treg cells
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data showing synergistic effects.

claim: Antigen-specific targeting of VAT-localized Treg cells could eventually be a strategy for improving metabolic disease.
source: These studies suggest that antigen-specific targeting of VAT-localized Treg cells could eventually be a strategy for improving metabolic disease.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the experimental findings.

claim: Foxp3+CD4+ T regulatory (Treg) cells restrain most types of immune response, guarding against run-away reactions.
source: Foxp3+CD4+ T regulatory (Treg) cells restrain most types of immune response, guarding against run-away reactions (Sakaguchi et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Tissue-Tregs have distinct transcriptomes, T-cell receptor (TCR) repertoires, and dependencies that optimally arm them to survive and function within a particular tissue.
source: 'Tissue-Tregs,' as they have been termed, have distinct transcriptomes, T-cell receptor (TCR) repertoires, and dependencies that optimally arm them to survive and function within a particular tissue.
evidence: This statement draws from established scientific knowledge about tissue-resident Treg cells.

claim: VAT-Treg cells control local and systemic inflammatory and metabolic indices.
source: According to a number of assays, VAT-Treg cells control local and systemic inflammatory and metabolic indices, promoting insulin sensitivity through influences on both inflammatory and parenchymal cells, notably macrophages and adipocytes.
evidence: This statement is based on prior experimental evidence from multiple assays.

claim: VAT-Treg cells promote insulin sensitivity through influences on both inflammatory and parenchymal cells, notably macrophages and adipocytes.
source: According to a number of assays, VAT-Treg cells control local and systemic inflammatory and metabolic indices, promoting insulin sensitivity through influences on both inflammatory and parenchymal cells, notably macrophages and adipocytes.
evidence: This statement is based on prior experimental evidence.

claim: VAT-Treg cells have a distinct transcriptome, driven primarily by the 'master-regulator' of adipocyte differentiation, PPARγ.
source: Like other tissue-Treg populations, VAT-Treg cells have a distinct transcriptome, driven primarily by the 'master-regulator' of adipocyte differentiation, PPARγ (Cipolletta et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: VAT-Treg cells display a distinct, clonally expanded TCR repertoire that exhibits signs of clonal selection.
source: They also display a distinct, clonally expanded TCR repertoire that exhibits signs of clonal selection (Feuerer et al., 2009; Kolodin et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The critical importance of the TCR for the accumulation and function of VAT-Treg cells was established using the vTreg53 TCR-transgenic (tg) mouse line.
source: The critical importance of the TCR for the accumulation and function of VAT-Treg cells was recently established using the vTreg53 TCR-transgenic (tg) mouse line, which has a TCR repertoire highly skewed for the specificity displayed by an expanded VAT-Treg clone (vTreg53) (Li et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: The vTreg53 TCR does not depend on the lipid-presenting CD1d molecule.
source: However, beyond its lack of dependence on the lipid-presenting CD1d molecule (Kolodin et al., 2015), little is known about the antigen(s) recognized by VAT-Treg cells.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Very few peptide antigens that selectively activate Treg cells have been identified.
source: More generally, the question of the antigen specificity of Treg cells remains open because very few peptide antigens that selectively activate them have been identified.
evidence: This statement reflects the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: De novo identification of cognate peptides for TCRs of interest is notoriously challenging.
source: De novo identification of cognate peptides for TCRs of interest is still notoriously challenging and apart from a few examples for testis-cancer antigens and self-peptides recognized by neonatal thymic Treg cells, the identity of Treg TCR ligands remains elusive (Leonard et al., 2017; Stadinski et al., 2019; Wang et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work and reflects the current state of the field.

claim: Antigen-specific activation appears to elicit stronger responses in autoimmunity or graft rejection treatment compared to polyspecific stimulation.
source: Furthermore, while polyspecific stimulation can produce Treg-mediated suppressive activity, antigen-specific activation appears to elicit stronger responses in autoimmunity or graft rejection treatment (DuPage and Bluestone, 2016; Tang et al., 2004; Yamazaki et al., 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: A single-chain construct composed of a 13-mer peptide, p3K, fused to the β1α1 domains and a c-Myc tag was designed for yeast surface expression.
source: Based on previous work on the peptide-Ek and other pMHC yeast libraries (Birnbaum et al., 2014; Brophy et al., 2003; Shusta et al., 1999), we designed a single-chain construct composed of a 13-mer peptide, p3K, fused to the β1α1 domains and a c-Myc tag, connected by suitable Gly-Ser linkers, in-frame with the Aga2 protein for expression at the yeast surface (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a methodological description supported by references to prior work and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The initial peptide-Ab construct was expressed at the yeast surface but could not bind to the cognate YAe-62.8 TCR, suggesting misfolding.
source: While we were able to observe expression of this construct at the yeast surface, we could not detect binding to the cognate YAe-62.8 TCR (YAe)(Dai et al., 2008), suggesting that the peptide-Ab construct was misfolded (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: A yeast library expressing randomly inserted mutations in the mini peptide-Ab construct was generated using error-prone PCR.
source: To overcome this issue, we generated a yeast library expressing a small number of randomly inserted mutations in the mini peptide-Ab construct using an error-prone polymerase chain reaction strategy (PCR; up to 3 to 5 mutations per kbp), which we then selected with the YAe TCR.
evidence: This is a methodological description of the experimental approach.

claim: Sequencing of isolated clones after 4 rounds of selection revealed two single-point mutations in the β-chain: Leu67Val and His46Tyr.
source: Sequencing of the isolated clones after 4 rounds of selection using TCR-coupled streptavidin beads revealed two single-point mutations in the β-chain of all sequenced clones: Leu67Val and His46Tyr (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by sequencing data and shown in figures.

claim: The two mutant residues (Leu67Val and His46Tyr) were found to be outside of the peptide-Ab/TCR interface based on crystal structures.
source: Furthermore, based on crystal structures for TCR interactions with cognate peptide-Ab molecules, the two mutant residues were found to be outside of the peptide-Ab/TCR interface (Figure 1A; Dai et al., 2008; Liu et al., 2002; Yin et al., 2011).
evidence: This is an inference based on structural data from cited prior work and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: In each round of TCR-selection, the fraction of c-Myc and TCR-tetramer positive cells increased, suggesting enrichment of a particular group of peptides.
source: In each round of TCR-selection, the fraction of c-Myc and TCR-tetramer (coupled to streptavidin, TCR-SA) positive cells increased, suggesting the enrichment of a particular group of peptides (Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by flow cytometry data shown in figures.

claim: Deep sequencing revealed strong enrichment for a group of closely related peptides after YAe TCR selection.
source: Deep sequencing of the DNA region encoding the peptide sequence from the isolated yeast clones for each of the four consecutive rounds of selection revealed a strong enrichment for a group of closely related peptides (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by deep sequencing data shown in Figure 1C,D.

claim: Nearly all peptides enriched by YAe TCR selection contained a Lys in the central, TCR-facing, p5 position.
source: For example, nearly all peptides contained a Lys in the central, TCR-facing, p5 position, a residue that is critical for recognition by the YAe TCR (Figure 1C,D; Dai et al., 2008; Huseby et al., 2005).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by deep sequencing data and citations to prior work.

claim: Substitution of the central Lys residue at p5 by a Leu residue eliminated TCR-SA binding.
source: To confirm that the observed TCR-SA binding was strictly peptide-dependent, we substituted the central Lys residue at p5 by a Leu residue. This single-point mutation eliminated TCR-SA staining (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The fraction of c-Myc-tag positive cells increased from ~29% in the naïve library to ~57% by the 4th round of the vTreg53 TCR selection.
source: The fraction of c-Myc-tag positive cells increased from ~29% in the naïve library to ~57% by the 4th round of the vTreg53 TCR selection (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by flow cytometry data shown in figures.

claim: Deep sequencing of the four rounds of vTreg53 TCR selection revealed strong enrichment of a group of highly similar peptides.
source: Despite this result, deep sequencing of the four rounds of selection revealed strong enrichment of a group of highly similar peptides (Figure 2B–D and Supplementary File 1).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by deep sequencing data shown in figures.

claim: Around 90% of all peptides found in the 4th round of vTreg53 TCR selection had the KGPHAVQ/A sequence from p2 to p8.
source: Around 90% of all peptides found in the 4th round of selection had the KGPHAVQ/A sequence from p2 to p8.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from deep sequencing analysis.

claim: Lys at p2 and Val at p7 were present in all peptides enriched by vTreg53 TCR selection.
source: Lys at p2, and Val at p7 were present in all peptides, while the p5 position was dominated by the closely related His or Arg residues (Figure 2B–D).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from deep sequencing analysis shown in figures.

claim: The p5 position in peptides enriched by vTreg53 TCR selection was dominated by the closely related His or Arg residues.
source: Lys at p2, and Val at p7 were present in all peptides, while the p5 position was dominated by the closely related His or Arg residues (Figure 2B–D).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from deep sequencing analysis shown in figures.

claim: Positive vTreg53 TCR-SA staining was detected for a single clone of peptide-Ab displaying the most enriched peptide: LMFKGPHAVQAVG.
source: Furthermore, positive vTreg53 TCR-SA staining was detected for a single clone of peptide-Ab displaying the most enriched peptide: LMFKGPHAVQAVG (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Fat7 and Fat15 were both able to up-regulate CD69 expression following stimulation of Jurkat T cells transduced with the vTreg53 TCR.
source: Fat7 (yellow in Figure 3A,B) and Fat15 (magenta in Figure 3B) were both able to up-regulate CD69 expression following stimulation of Jurkat T cells transduced with the vTreg53 TCR in culture with peptide-pulsed K562-Ab cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by flow cytometry data shown in figures.

claim: The majority of single-point mutants based on Fat7 or Fat15 eliminated activation or had a negligible effect compared with the original peptides.
source: For both peptide libraries, the majority of single-point mutants eliminated activation or had a negligible effect when compared with the original Fat7 or Fat15 peptides (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from the functional screen shown in figures.

claim: Single-point mutations based on Fat15, particularly those in the p7 position, led to a marked increase in CD69 up-regulation.
source: However, a few single-point mutations based on Fat15, particularly those present in the p7 position, led to a marked increase in CD69 up-regulation (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from the functional screen shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Mutation of Val to Met or Trp at p7 induced the highest levels of CD69 expression.
source: Mutation of Val to Met or Trp at p7 induced the highest levels of CD69 expression (Figure 3B,C).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from the functional screen shown in figures.

claim: The substitution of Pro to Leu in p4 resulted in an increase in CD69 expression.
source: The substitution of Pro to Leu in p4, an anchor position, also resulted in an increase in CD69 expression.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from the functional screen.

claim: Fat1562 showed a decrease in EC50 to 14.3 µM compared to 40.7 µM for Fat15.
source: Titration of Fat15 and the peptides with Met at p7 (Fat1562) and Leu at p4 and Trp at p7 (Fat2564) revealed a decrease in EC50 from 40.7 µM for Fat15 to 14.3 µM for Fat1562 and 8.9 µM for Fat2564 (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from dose-response analysis shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Fat2564 showed a decrease in EC50 to 8.9 µM compared to 40.7 µM for Fat15.
source: Titration of Fat15 and the peptides with Met at p7 (Fat1562) and Leu at p4 and Trp at p7 (Fat2564) revealed a decrease in EC50 from 40.7 µM for Fat15 to 14.3 µM for Fat1562 and 8.9 µM for Fat2564 (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from dose-response analysis shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The CD69 Emax was increased by ~3 fold for Fat1562 and almost 5-fold for Fat2564 when compared with Fat15.
source: The CD69 Emax was also increased by ~3 fold for Fat1562 and almost 5-fold for Fat2564 when compared with Fat15 (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from dose-response analysis shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Fat1562 and Fat2564 induced a 4.1- and 8.7-fold increase in CD25 Emax, respectively, over Fat15.
source: The increase in activation for Fat1562 and Fat2564 was further confirmed by CD25 up-regulation, where these peptides induced a 4.1- and a 8.7-fold increase in Emax, respectively, over Fat15 (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from dose-response analysis shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Fat1562 and Fat2564 exhibited the slowest koff and highest affinity (Kd ~5.9 µM and 347 nM, respectively).
source: While all peptides appeared to show fast on-rates, typical for TCR/pMHC interactions, Fat1562 and Fat2562 exhibited the slowest koff and highest affinity (Kd ~5.9 µM and 347 nM, respectively; Figure 3F).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from surface plasmon resonance measurements shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Fat7 and Fat15 showed both fast kon and koff and a Kd of ~34.7 µM and ~32.8 µM, respectively.
source: Fat7 and Fat15 showed both fast kon and koff and a Kd of ~34.7 µM and ~32.8 µM, respectively (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from surface plasmon resonance measurements shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Fat1562-Ab showed a marked increase in the fraction of tetramer-positive cells over Fat15-Ab.
source: Furthermore, the Fat15-Ab and Fat1562-Ab tetramers readily stained vTreg53-TCR-transduced Jurkat T cells, with Fat1562-Ab showing a marked increase in the fraction of tetramer-positive cells over Fat15-Ab, in good agreement with the binding-affinity measurements (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: At a concentration of 1 µM, all SPs induced robust proliferation and activation of TCR-tg Treg cells.
source: At a concentration of 1 µM, all SPs induced robust proliferation and activation of TCR-tg Treg cells, as measured by dilution of the CellTrace Violet dye (Figure 4A and B) and upregulation of CD44 (Figure 4C), respectively.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from in vitro Treg cell stimulation assays shown in figures.

claim: Fat1562 induced the strongest down-regulation of CD62L at 1 µM concentration.
source: Fat1562 induced the strongest down-regulation of CD62L, while Fat7 dampened CD62L levels only moderately at this high concentration (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from in vitro Treg cell stimulation assays shown in Figure 4D.

claim: At a low dose of 0.01 μM, Fat7 was unable to promote any further proliferation and up-regulation of CD44 expression compared with the control group.
source: In agreement with this finding, at a low dose of 0.01 μM, Fat7 was unable to promote any further proliferation and up-regulation of CD44 expression compared with the control group (no peptide; Figure 4A–C).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from in vitro Treg cell stimulation assays shown in figures.

claim: At 0.01 μM concentration, Fat1562 induced the strongest proliferation and down-regulation of CD62L in TCR-tg Treg cells.
source: Again, at this concentration, Fat1562 induced the strongest proliferation and down-regulation of CD62L in TCR-tg Treg cells (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from in vitro Treg cell stimulation assays shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Fat2564 had a relatively weak potency for primary TCR-tg Treg cells, comparable with that of Fat7.
source: Interestingly, Fat2564, the strongest SP for the vTreg53 TCR in the Jurkat system, had a relatively weak potency, which was comparable with that of Fat7 for primary TCR-tg Treg cells (Figure 4A–D), indicating that the optimal threshold for peptide stimulation was different for different T cell subtypes, or between primary cells and cell lines.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from in vitro Treg cell stimulation assays shown in figures.

claim: The optimal threshold for peptide stimulation was different for different T cell subtypes, or between primary cells and cell lines.
source: Interestingly, Fat2564, the strongest SP for the vTreg53 TCR in the Jurkat system, had a relatively weak potency, which was comparable with that of Fat7 for primary TCR-tg Treg cells (Figure 4A–D), indicating that the optimal threshold for peptide stimulation was different for different T cell subtypes, or between primary cells and cell lines.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the differential responses of Jurkat cells versus primary Treg cells to the same peptides.

claim: Immunization with CFA/Fat1562 led to robust proliferation of transferred Vα2+Vβ4+ (clonotype+) Treg cells in the spleen three days after transfer.
source: Injection of CFA alone led to very little proliferation of transferred Treg cells in the spleen three days after transfer. However, when the recipient mice were immunized with CFA/Fat1562, transferred Vα2+Vβ4+ (clonotype+) Treg cells underwent robust proliferation (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from in vivo Treg cell transfer and immunization experiments shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Following transfer into B6 mice, vTreg53 TCR-tg Treg cells preferentially accumulated specifically in the VAT of recipient mice over the course of several weeks.
source: We have previously reported that following transfer into B6 mice, vTreg53 TCR-tg Treg cells preferentially accumulated specifically in the VAT of recipient mice over the course of several weeks.
evidence: This statement refers to prior published work by the authors.

claim: Immunization with Fat1562 induced a 6- to 7-fold expansion of TCR-tg Treg cells in the Spl/LN, compared with adjuvant alone.
source: Immunization with Fat1562 induced a 6- to 7-fold expansion of TCR-tg Treg cells in the Spl/LN, compared with adjuvant alone.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from in vivo Treg cell transfer and immunization experiments.

claim: Immunization with Fat1562 induced an even more substantial expansion (>25 fold) of clonotype+ Treg cells in the VAT.
source: Remarkably, it induced an even more substantial expansion (>25 fold) of clonotype+ Treg cells in the VAT (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from in vivo Treg cell transfer and immunization experiments shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Clonotype+ VAT Treg cells from mice immunized with adjuvant alone showed enriched expression of the previously defined VAT-Treg up-signature.
source: As expected, compared with those in the lymphoid organs, clonotype+ VAT Treg cells from mice immunized with adjuvant alone showed enriched expression of the previously defined VAT-Treg up-signature, while the down-signature was under-represented (Figure 5A, left).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claim: In mice immunized with adjuvant plus Fat1562, clonotype+ VAT Treg cells still exhibited preferential expression of VAT-Treg signature genes.
source: In mice immunized with adjuvant plus Fat1562, clonotype+ VAT Treg cells still exhibited preferential expression of VAT-Treg signature genes (Figure 5A, right), indicating that the VAT Treg cells expanded by Fat1562 preserved the typical VAT-Treg characteristics.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The VAT Treg cells expanded by Fat1562 preserved the typical VAT-Treg characteristics.
source: In mice immunized with adjuvant plus Fat1562, clonotype+ VAT Treg cells still exhibited preferential expression of VAT-Treg signature genes (Figure 5A, right), indicating that the VAT Treg cells expanded by Fat1562 preserved the typical VAT-Treg characteristics.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Fat1562-stimulated VAT-Treg cells showed significant enrichment in pathways and transcripts related to cell division.
source: In agreement with the remarkable expansion of clonotype+ Treg cells in VAT by Fat1562 immunization, Fat1562-stimulated VAT-Treg cells showed significant enrichment in pathways and transcripts related to cell division (E2F targets, G2M checkpoint, MYC targets, Mitotic spindle) and glycolysis (Figure 5B&D, left).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from GSEA analysis of RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5B&D.

claim: Fat1562-stimulated VAT-Treg cells showed significant enrichment in pathways and transcripts related to glycolysis.
source: In agreement with the remarkable expansion of clonotype+ Treg cells in VAT by Fat1562 immunization, Fat1562-stimulated VAT-Treg cells showed significant enrichment in pathways and transcripts related to cell division (E2F targets, G2M checkpoint, MYC targets, Mitotic spindle) and glycolysis (Figure 5B&D, left).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from GSEA analysis of RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5B&D.

claim: Several Treg signature genes such as Lag3 and Tigit were upregulated in Fat1562-stimulated VAT-Treg cells.
source: Several Treg signature genes such as Lag3 and Tigit were also upregulated in Fat1562-stimulated VAT-Treg cells (Figure 5D, left).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 5D.

claim: In lymphoid organs, antigen stimulation led to increased expression of genes associated with responses to inflammatory cytokines (IFNα, IFNγ, and TNFα).
source: On the other hand, in lymphoid organs, antigen stimulation led to increased expression of genes associated with responses to inflammatory cytokines (IFNα, IFNγ, and TNFα), likely reflecting changes in the microenvironment of lymphoid organs with peptide immunization.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from RNA-seq analysis with an inference about the biological meaning.

claim: In lymphoid organs, antigen stimulation led to enrichment of genes involved in cholesterol homeostasis (e.g., Pparg, Nfil3, and Srebf2).
source: But most interestingly, we observed an enrichment of genes involved in cholesterol homeostasis (e.g., Pparg, Nfil3, and Srebf2), a hallmark of VAT-Treg cells (Figure 5B&D, right).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 5B&D.

claim: Pparg mRNA levels were significantly increased in Spl/LN Treg cells when stimulated by Fat1562 in vivo but remained substantially lower than in Fat1562-stimulated VAT Treg cells.
source: Pparg mRNA levels were significantly increased in Spl/LN Treg cells when stimulated by Fat1562 in vivo but remained substantially lower than in Fat1562-stimulated VAT Treg cells (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Out of 10 wild-type B6 mice immunized with Fat1562, three showed detectable expansion of the Fat1562/Ab tetramer+ Treg population in the Spl/LN and VAT.
source: Interestingly, out of the 10 mice immunized, three showed detectable expansion of the Fat1562/Ab tetramer+ Treg population in the Spl/LN and VAT, characteristic of the high variability of endogenous Treg cells' responses to specific peptide immunization (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B&C).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from in vivo immunization experiments shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B&C.

claim: In each of the three wild-type mice that responded to Fat1562 immunization, the Fat1562/Ab tetramer+ Treg population was almost entirely monoclonal.
source: Surprisingly, in each of the three mice, the Fat1562/Ab tetramer+ Treg population was almost entirely monoclonal (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from single-cell TCR sequencing shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Within each wild-type mouse, the Spl/LNs and VAT Treg clones responding to Fat1562 had the same CDR3α and CDR3β.
source: Within each mouse, the Spl/LNs and VAT Treg clones had the same CDR3α and CDR3β.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from single-cell TCR sequencing.

claim: Across different wild-type mice, none of the Fat1562-reactive Treg clones was shared, and their CDR3 sequences did not show any obvious similarity.
source: However, across different mice, none of the clones was shared, and their CDR3 sequences did not show any obvious similarity.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from single-cell TCR sequencing.

claim: One of the Fat1562/Ab-reactive clones had a CDR3α and a CDR3β highly reminiscent of the vTreg53 CDR3s, with the exact same CDR3α sequence and only one amino acid difference in CDR3β.
source: Nevertheless, one of the Fat1562/Ab-reactive clones had a CDR3α and a CDR3β highly reminiscent of the vTreg53 CDR3s, with the exact same CDR3α sequence and only one amino acid difference in CDR3β (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from single-cell TCR sequencing shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Chronic, low grade inflammation in VAT is one of the major drivers of obesity-induced insulin resistance.
source: Chronic, low grade inflammation in VAT is one of the major drivers of obesity-induced insulin resistance, and VAT Treg cells are important for keeping this inflammation in check.
evidence: This statement draws from established scientific knowledge about obesity and insulin resistance.

claim: VAT Treg cells are important for keeping VAT inflammation in check.
source: Chronic, low grade inflammation in VAT is one of the major drivers of obesity-induced insulin resistance, and VAT Treg cells are important for keeping this inflammation in check.
evidence: This statement draws from established scientific knowledge about VAT Treg cell function.

claim: Immunization with Fat1562 led to a 5- to 10-fold expansion of the transferred TCR-Tg Treg cells in the spleen.
source: As expected, immunization with Fat1562 led to a 5- to 10-fold expansion of the transferred TCR-Tg Treg cells in the spleen, particularly for clonotype+ Treg cells (Figure 6B–D).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from in vivo experiments shown in Figure 6B–D.

claim: Donor-derived cells contributed less than 2% of the total Treg pool in the spleen of recipient mice after Fat1562 immunization.
source: However, donor-derived cells still contributed less than 2% of the total Treg pool in the spleen of recipient mice.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from in vivo experiments.

claim: The total number of splenic Treg cells in recipient mice did not show a significant increase with Fat1562 immunization.
source: As a result, the total number of splenic Treg cells in recipient mice did not show a significant increase with immunization (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from in vivo experiments shown in Figure 6F.

claim: With adjuvant alone, transferred TCR-tg Treg cells preferentially accumulated in VAT compared with the spleen, but made up less than 5% of the total VAT-Treg compartment.
source: As expected, with adjuvant alone, transferred TCR-tg Treg cells preferentially accumulated in VAT compared with the spleen, but still made up less than 5% of the total VAT-Treg compartment in recipient mice (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from in vivo experiments shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Immunization with adjuvant plus Fat1562 led to substantial expansion of clonotype+ TCR-tg Treg cells, reaching almost half of the entire VAT-Treg pool in recipient mice.
source: In contrast, immunization with adjuvant plus Fat1562 led to substantial expansion of clonotype+ TCR-tg Treg cells, reaching almost half of the entire VAT-Treg pool in recipient mice (Figure 6B,C and E).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from in vivo experiments shown in Figure 6B,C and E.

claim: The total number of VAT Treg cells was significantly elevated after Fat1562 immunization.
source: As a consequence, the total number of VAT Treg cells was also significantly elevated (Figure 6G).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from in vivo experiments shown in Figure 6G.

claim: Obesity promotes differentiation/activation of pro-inflammatory immunocytes, particularly CD11chi macrophages.
source: In lean mice, VAT is enriched for anti-inflammatory immunocyte subsets, while obesity promotes differentiation/activation of pro-inflammatory immunocytes, particularly CD11chi macrophages.
evidence: This statement draws from established scientific knowledge about obesity and immune cell composition.

claim: Immunization with Fat1562 significantly increased the proportion of eosinophils in VAT.
source: Consistent with an important function of VAT-Treg cells in maintaining the balance between different types of immunocytes in the local microenvironment, immunization with Fat1562 significantly increased the proportion of eosinophils while reducing the frequency of CD11chi pro-inflammatory macrophages (Figure 6H; gating strategy is shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 6H.

claim: Immunization with Fat1562 reduced the frequency of CD11chi pro-inflammatory macrophages in VAT.
source: Consistent with an important function of VAT-Treg cells in maintaining the balance between different types of immunocytes in the local microenvironment, immunization with Fat1562 significantly increased the proportion of eosinophils while reducing the frequency of CD11chi pro-inflammatory macrophages (Figure 6H; gating strategy is shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 6H.

claim: Fat1562 immunization of HFD-fed B6 mice that received vTreg53 Treg cells improved insulin sensitivity.
source: In agreement with dampened VAT inflammation, and although body weights were similar (Figure 7A), Fat1562 immunization of HFD-fed B6 mice that received vTreg53 Treg cells improved insulin sensitivity (Figure 7B and C, Figure 7—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is an experimental finding from insulin tolerance tests shown in figures.

claim: Fat1562 immunization of HFD-fed B6 mice that received vTreg53 Treg cells promoted glucose tolerance.

claim: Fat1562 immunization of HFD-fed B6 mice that received vTreg53 Treg cells reduced fasting plasma insulin levels.

evidence: This is an experimental finding from insulin measurements shown in Figure 7F.

claim: TNFα levels in VAT increase with obesity.

claim: Co-administration of Fat1562 and anti-TNFα suppressed pro-inflammatory macrophages.
source: Co-administration of Fat1562 and anti-TNFα strikingly increased VAT-Treg cells, suppressed pro-inflammatory macrophages, and strongly promoted insulin sensitivity (Figure 7H–K).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from in vivo experiments shown in Figure 7H–K.

claim: Co-administration of Fat1562 and anti-TNFα strongly promoted insulin sensitivity.
source: Co-administration of Fat1562 and anti-TNFα strikingly increased VAT-Treg cells, suppressed pro-inflammatory macrophages, and strongly promoted insulin sensitivity (Figure 7H–K).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from in vivo experiments shown in Figure 7H–K.

claim: TCR expression is essential for Treg cell function.
source: Importantly, several studies demonstrated that TCR expression is essential for Treg cell function (Levine et al., 2014; Schmidt et al., 2015)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The TCR repertoire of Treg cells can recognize self- as well as foreign peptides.
source: and that the TCR repertoire of these cells can recognize self- as well as foreign peptides (Jordan et al., 2001; Lee et al., 2012; Pacholczyk et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: TCR stimulation shapes various Treg-cell phenotypes.
source: Furthermore, TCR stimulation shapes various Treg-cell phenotypes (Zemmour et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Surrogate peptides can promote clonal Treg-cell proliferation without compromising key features of the VAT-Treg transcriptome.
source: Our results suggest that SPs can promote clonal Treg-cell proliferation without compromising key features of the VAT-Treg transcriptome, while suppressing HFD-induced VAT inflammation and improving insulin sensitivity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings presented in the manuscript.

claim: Surrogate peptides can suppress HFD-induced VAT inflammation.
source: Our results suggest that SPs can promote clonal Treg-cell proliferation without compromising key features of the VAT-Treg transcriptome, while suppressing HFD-induced VAT inflammation and improving insulin sensitivity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings presented in the manuscript.

claim: Surrogate peptides can improve insulin sensitivity.
source: Our results suggest that SPs can promote clonal Treg-cell proliferation without compromising key features of the VAT-Treg transcriptome, while suppressing HFD-induced VAT inflammation and improving insulin sensitivity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings presented in the manuscript.

claim: The TCR has a rather reduced cross-reactivity and shows a poly-specific response.
source: Recent work suggests that the TCR has a rather reduced cross-reactivity and shows, instead, a poly-specific response (Birnbaum et al., 2014; Wucherpfennig et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The TCR mostly recognizes a small, closely related, number of peptides.
source: In other words, the TCR mostly recognizes a small, closely related, number of peptides.
evidence: This is an inference based on the concept of poly-specificity mentioned in prior work.

claim: The SPs identified using the vTreg53 TCR failed to fully align with a peptide region from the mouse proteome.
source: However, the SPs identified using the vTreg53 TCR failed to fully align with a peptide region from the mouse proteome and, despite extensive effort, we could not deorphanize the vTreg53 TCR with an endogenous antigen.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from attempts to identify endogenous ligands.

claim: Candidate wild-type peptides relatively similar to Fat7 or Fat15 failed to activate vTreg53 cells.
source: Furthermore, candidate wild-type peptides relatively similar to Fat7 or Fat15 failed to activate vTreg53 cells.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from attempts to identify endogenous ligands.

claim: Altered peptide ligands have long been used to elicit more potent T cell responses.
source: Altered peptide ligands, or SPs, have long been used to elicit more potent T cell responses, and often represent a useful approach to circumvent poor TCR recognition due to weak peptide binding to MHC, multiple peptide registers, lower avidity or poor TCR/pMHC affinity (Sloan-Lancaster and Allen, 1996).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Surrogate peptides have proven to be a valuable tool to explore key aspects of peptide recognition and the T cell response.
source: Furthermore, SPs have proven to be a valuable tool to explore key aspects of peptide recognition and the T cell response (Evavold and Allen, 1991; Evavold et al., 1995).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Surrogate peptides were shown to drastically suppress autoimmune responses during experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis.
source: More recently, SPs were shown to drastically suppress autoimmune responses during experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis, a murine model for multiple sclerosis (Saligrama et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Peptide-induced expansion of the Treg population was restricted to those cells displaying a very small number of TCRs.
source: First, peptide-induced expansion of the Treg population was restricted to those cells displaying a very small number of TCRs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings on clonal expansion.

claim: Long-term HFD feeding induces a VAT microenvironment that is highly toxic to VAT-Treg cells, partially due to increased level of TNFα.
source: Previous studies showed that long-term HFD feeding is able to induce a VAT microenvironment that is highly toxic to VAT-Treg cells, partially due to increased level of TNFα (Cipolletta et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: There has been substantial interest in harnessing the power of Treg cells to therapeutic ends, in particular for the amelioration of graft-versus-host, autoimmune or inflammatory diseases.
source: There has been substantial interest in harnessing the power of Treg cells to therapeutic ends, in particular for the amelioration of graft-versus-host, autoimmune or inflammatory diseases (Sakaguchi et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work and reflects the current state of the field.

claim: Antigen-specific stimulation of tissue-resident Treg cells has been found to be more effective at suppressing immune responses than polyclonal stimulation.
source: While polyclonal stimulation of Treg cells readily induces broad clonal expansion, antigen-specific stimulation of tissue-resident Treg cells has been found to be more effective at suppressing immune responses.
evidence: This statement draws from established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: In murine models of type-1 diabetes, antigen stimulation of Treg cells performed better at ameliorating diabetes progression than polyclonal Treg cells.
source: In murine models of type-1 diabetes, antigen stimulation of Treg cells performed better at ameliorating diabetes progression than polyclonal Treg cells (Tang et al., 2004; Yamazaki et al., 2006)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Similar results were found in humanized-mouse transplant models comparing antigen-specific versus polyclonal Treg stimulation.
source: and similar results were found in humanized-mouse transplant models (Putnam et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Non-lymphoid-tissue Treg cells will be a more effective source than their lymphoid-organ counterparts for therapeutic applications.
source: Moreover, recent data on the phenotypic distinction of non-lymphoid-tissue Treg cells argue that they will be a more effective source then their lymphoid-organ counterparts (Panduro et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work and represents an inference about therapeutic potential.

claim: Surrogate peptides may offer a simpler and viable alternative to self-antigens in promoting local, tissue-specific, Treg expansion and immunosuppressive activity.
source: Surrogate peptides may offer a simpler and viable alternative to self-antigens in promoting local, tissue-specific, Treg expansion and immunosuppressive activity.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the experimental findings and potential therapeutic applications.
